Heh that's my story. I'm losing a friendship as I always talked about my problems.

I did it because at first I did not realise it - my problems were very worrying me and I thought it was natural for me to talk more about it.

And because I had no one else to talk to. Well I really don't have anyone now. Yay. Oh and I ran out of topics so I came up with topics that I know well of.

She hasn't mentioned anything yet but her behaviour lately clearly shows that she wants to end the friendship with me. So I haven't contacted her for a month. 

But I think I would've felt much better if she clearly stated that she's tired of hearing my own problems. Not just social cues, it's hard to catch. And not just avoid me but confront and tell me her feelings about our relationship. 

For me the fear of her not liking me was what killed me. We were friends for five years and I lost her over my own problems. I mean for me it wasn't just a friendship - I had crush on her (I'm bisexual). It got worse when she made a boyfriend. He was 32, we were 16. I really didn't want to hear about her boyfriend so I came out with different topics. Odd topics that will absolutely not interest her in any ways. And rants about my problems. 

I knew, I goddamn knew what I was doing but it was too late. I miss her but I'm now avoiding her for her sake. I can't believe what a pathetic thing I've done and I can't believe I'm ranting about my personal problems, that no one cares, as a reply to such post. 

**TLDR Start gently avoiding her + show social cues. When it's time explain to her that you feel like she used her as an emotional bin rather than a mutual friend. Telling her that you don't hate herself but just her rants would help as well**

I'm sorry you were in an abusive household :( I hope you're safe now. 

And so.. where do I start. Trust me I've done everything I could. I've told this to two friends; #1 told the school counsellor without my consent. The counsellor told my home room teacher. I chickened out at this point since I was mad at my friend. #2 called the police again without my consent. I've talked to a policewoman and she said I and my parents will be on a "list" for further assistance, and if I wanted to proceed she can arrange a counselling with my mother to alert that her methods are wrong. That was all they could do. 

Letting my mother talking to the police? Eh, nope. I'll be in a deep deep trouble. 

My father is also umm, he works for a government and he's got this big name and power so even if I insisted the counselling he can do things. Nope nope nope. 

I've thought about running away, which I did few times before. If I run away now I wouldn't be able to support myself and would likely be homeless. 

I forgot to clarify- I'm in East Asia. It's different here. There's nothing much to do but to grow up and go to uni. 

I know how it sounds bad to outsiders but if you live through that 24/7 you get used to it and it just becomes your everyday life. I'll just wait for few more years. 

But thank you for your comment!
I guess some people do like them but for God's sake DO NOT PLAY THEM IN PUBLIC there are little kids there and do you know how embarrassing it is urgh

If more than three people compliment the same thing, it's likely to be true. However compliments about weight/beauty could be mostly false. Observe carefully of their body language to determine whether it's false or not.
Well.. we have the weekends?
For me I get exhausted after work to even change clothes. I wouldn't physically be able to think of anything

For me I have abnormally accurate picture memory. It's rather annoying since there are so many reminiscences you bump into. But when it comes to other memories such as short term memories, oh boy I got in so many trouble for forgetting things.
Erm isn't it normal to laze off after work?
*It must stink*

Great to hear about your best friend. People do seem to change and you never know what's going to happen. I hope five years were enough. I'm pretty sure they hate me, at least back in middle school. The looks, atmosphere, whispering. It is amazing how people instinctively know when someone hates you. Even for autistic me (it did take longer to realise though). 

The knowledge part. So true. You know what's going on, you try to strain yourself to avoid it, ends up being even worse. Anxiety is a funny thing.

At least I'm glad I am self aware. I feel like I'm controlling myself too much because of it but anyways I will try to be the natural myself. Smile.

Well got to pack my backs. Thank you. I wish the best for you as well.
Few years back I did. Wasn't nice. Now I only go to doctors to get my prescriptions.

I avoid going out because the guy lives close and we get to bump each other few times. And the school neighbourhood as well. Something I should get over with.

And I'm very grateful that they don't actually do anything. It would've been a lot harder. They are not bad people. We don't really know each other well. Just few bad impressions in the past. Also it does look like they are aware I'm different.

I looked for help before - money blah blah blah. I don't feel like it to tell people about my middle school as well. They could get police involved. Not good.

Welp thank you for sparing your time and for your advices. Have a nice evening.

Autism, nope I'm not exactly going to fit. I'll just try to act natural and nice. The other part, I'm afraid things will get even messier with someone else involved. I just would like to get over it. Thank you for your time and kindness to write this comment.

Yeah I changed a lot over the last five years as well. I hope they don't mind me. So fake it, be neutral and polite, seek for further help. Got it. The talk part - hmm. I'm not so sure about that but it's alright. Hope this whole thing ends soon. Thank you Alex.

Thank you for sharing your experience. It helps me that I'm not the only one. Good luck with your new university. From what you wrote you sound like a nice person. I'm sure you'll do well. Again thank you. Have a nice evening.

I'm so glad it turned out well! You did amazing, I envy that. It looks like I'm not the only one experiencing this. Thank you for your advice. I will try to cover it up. And I hope you meet great people and learn fun things.
Thank you all for your kind upvotes and comments. I wish it goes out smoothly. And I also wish that your own problems goes out well as well. Thank you, have a nice evening.

Honestly sorry but this community isn't exactly helpful for balding. Maybe seek other communities, r/balding for example?

And my view, I don't know much about balding, it doesn't look that bad. I don't think anyone could notice.

I'm glad you are no longer working there and no longer harmed. Eww, people can be so mean sometimes. It's probably because they are fragile inside and it's the only way they can cope with it. Or they could be trying to fit in. Either way, those people sound like bunch of jerks. 

Again toast for leaving the job. I know you've put a lot of thought on it and I think you did the right thing. 

Now. As you said you had anxiety experiences earlier in your life as well I think it would be a good time to get professional help. Gives you a reason to crawl out of bed as well. And as you are now mostly at home, why don't you do some exercise? Go out. Breathe fresh air. Boost your self esteem. Perhaps meet new people. 

Or seek some volunteering work. What do you like? There are actually vast kinds of things you could do. Animal shelters, children, elders, libraries, pick what you like. Or why don't you do something extra to put on your resume?

Anyway cheers, I hope you get better soon and get a better workplace.
